title: Bot is taking momentum/trend trades, not mean reversion trades
analysis: Of the 4 SUBMITTED/executed trades in this journal, 2 are clearly counter-strategy: NVDA (2026-05-15) fired 'RSI>65', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25 (trending)' — all momentum signals, the exact OPPOSITE of mean reversion — yet was submitted with signal_score=4. AAPL (2026-05-18) fired 'RSI>65', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25 (trending)', 'A_GRADE setup' — again pure momentum signals — yet was also submitted. The MSFT SELL (2026-05-18) fired only 'ADX<25' with signal_score=1, below threshold. Meanwhile, 6 REJECTED trades (MSFT x3, META x4) had legitimate mean reversion signals ('RSI<45', 'BelowMA20>1%', 'ADX<25') with R:R of 1.68–3.95, all rejected only because of the no-add-to-existing-position rule. The bot is executing the wrong signal type while blocking the correct ones.
rationale: The signal scoring system currently awards points for RSI>65 and AboveMA20>1% which are momentum confirmations, not mean reversion signals. These should either score zero or actively disqualify the trade. The current rules say 'If ADX > 30, do NOT take mean reversion signals' but the NVDA and AAPL trades had ADX>25 (trending) firing — the bot is submitting trades that violate the spirit of Rule 6 because the hard cutoff is 30, not 25. The mean reversion signals (RSI<45, BelowMA20) are firing correctly on META and MSFT but being blocked by position duplication, while wrong-direction momentum trades are getting through.

insight.why_now: 2 of 2 submitted BUY trades in this dataset fired RSI>65 and ADX>25 — textbook trend-following signals — while all 6 rejected mean reversion setups had R:R between 1.68 and 3.95 and proper oversold signals. The bot is systematically executing the wrong strategy.
insight.purpose: Ensure the signal scoring system only awards positive points for mean reversion signals and explicitly blocks trades where momentum/trend signals dominate the score.
insight.expected_effect: Eliminates counter-strategy entries. The NVDA and AAPL trades (momentum chases in trending conditions) would be blocked. The META/MSFT setups would score correctly as mean reversion candidates.
insight.risks: If RSI>65 and AboveMA20 were being used as a separate breakout sub-strategy intentionally, removing them breaks that. But per CLAUDE.md this bot is ONLY mean reversion — so those signals should never produce a BUY.

current_rule:
## SIGNAL SCORING (need 2+ to enter under medium_safety profile)
- RSI < 35: +2 points (strong oversold)
- RSI < 45: +1 point (mild oversold)
- Price below lower Bollinger Band: +1 point
- Price below MA20 by > 1%: +1 point
- ADX < 25 (ranging market): +1 point (regime confirmation)
proposed_rule:
## SIGNAL SCORING (need 2+ to enter under medium_safety profile)
- RSI < 35: +2 points (strong oversold)
- RSI < 45: +1 point (mild oversold)
- Price below lower Bollinger Band: +1 point
- Price below MA20 by > 1%: +1 point
- ADX < 25 (ranging market): +1 point (regime confirmation)

## SIGNAL DISQUALIFIERS — ANY of these immediately forces SKIP, overriding signal score
- RSI > 60: SKIP — price is overbought, not a mean reversion long setup
- Price above MA20 by > 1%: SKIP — price is extended above mean, not below it
- ADX > 25 AND rising: SKIP — trend is building; mean reversion entries fail in early trends
- Signals fired contain 'AboveMA20', 'RSI>65', or 'strong momentum': SKIP immediately

title: No-add-to-position rule is blocking the best setups — add pyramid/re-entry logic
analysis: 6 trades were REJECTED solely due to 'Already hold X shares — bot does not add to existing positions': MSFT x3 (May 14, signal_score=2, R:R 1.68–1.91) and META x4 (May 19, signal_score=4, R:R 3.10–3.36). The META rejections are particularly costly: 4 consecutive signals on May 19 with R:R averaging 3.18, oversold RSI<45, BelowMA20, ADX<25, and PositiveSentiment — all blocked. The account was running a day P&L of -$50 to -$144 during that window, suggesting the existing META position was underwater and additional entries at lower prices would have improved the average cost. MSFT signals were score=2 (minimum threshold) so borderline, but META at score=4 with R:R >3.0 represents genuine opportunity cost.
rationale: The blanket no-add rule prevents scaling into high-conviction setups when price moves further from the mean — exactly the scenario where mean reversion has the highest probability. A tiered re-entry rule (allow one add if signal score ≥ 4, R:R ≥ 2.5, and the new entry is at least 1x ATR below original entry) would capture the META-type setups while still blocking low-quality additions. Total position exposure would remain capped by the existing 10% max position size rule.

insight.why_now: 4 consecutive META rejections on May 19 with R:R 3.10–3.36 and score=4 represent the single largest identifiable opportunity cost block in this dataset. All 4 fired the same 4 signals, suggesting a persistent oversold condition that the bot correctly identified but could not act on.
insight.purpose: Allow one scale-in entry on existing positions when the setup is high-conviction (score ≥ 4) and price has moved meaningfully further from the mean, improving average entry and expected R-multiple.
insight.expected_effect: Unlocks ~6 blocked trades per 50-cycle window. For META-quality setups (R:R ~3.2, score=4), expected positive impact on total P&L. Would not increase max risk beyond existing 10% position cap if quantity is scaled to keep total position within limit.
insight.risks: Averaging into a losing position can amplify losses if the mean reversion fails. Must require strict conditions: new entry must be at least 1.0x ATR lower than original, combined position must not exceed 10% account, and signal score must be ≥ 4 (not 2).

current_rule: 3. MAX OPEN POSITIONS: Never hold more than 5 positions simultaneously (medium_safety).
proposed_rule: 3. MAX OPEN POSITIONS: Never hold more than 5 positions simultaneously (medium_safety). Re-entry / scale-in exception: A second entry in an existing position is permitted ONLY if ALL of the following are true: (a) signal_score ≥ 4, (b) risk_reward ≥ 2.5, (c) new entry price is at least 1.0x ATR below the original entry price, (d) combined shares would not push total position value above 10% of account, (e) no more than ONE scale-in per symbol per day. MSFT/META-type repeated signals at score=2 do NOT qualify for scale-in.

title: Lower ADX trend-block threshold from 30 to 25 to match signals already firing
analysis: Rule 6 currently blocks mean reversion entries when ADX > 30. However, both submitted BUY trades (NVDA on May 15 and AAPL on May 18) fired 'ADX>25 (trending)' as a positive signal rather than a disqualifier — meaning the bot's own signal detection identified trending conditions but still executed. The ADX scoring system already tracks ADX>25 as a regime warning, yet the hard block is set 5 points higher at ADX>30. This gap between detection (25) and blocking (30) creates a window where the bot correctly identifies a building trend but is not stopped from entering. The NVDA trade entered at $229.02 with ADX>25 trending — a mean reversion long in a confirmed uptrend, which is structurally high-risk.
rationale: Aligning the hard ADX block with the signal detection threshold eliminates the inconsistency. If the scoring system already treats ADX>25 as a regime warning worth flagging, the entry rule should respect that same level. ADX 25-30 is the 'building trend' zone where mean reversion has the lowest historical success rate — the signal is working against the position from the moment of entry. Dropping the threshold from 30 to 25 costs very few valid mean reversion setups (which should have ADX<25 to earn the +1 regime confirmation point anyway).

insight.why_now: Both SUBMITTED buys in this dataset had ADX>25 trending firing — meaning 100% of executed entries were in regime conditions that the scoring system itself flagged as non-ideal. The threshold gap between signal detection (25) and hard block (30) is directly responsible.
insight.purpose: Close the inconsistency between the signal scoring system and the hard trend filter. A trade that scores +1 for ADX<25 (ranging) should not be entered when ADX is actually >25.
insight.expected_effect: Would have blocked both the NVDA and AAPL BUY submissions in this dataset. Reduces counter-trend mean reversion entries. Minor reduction in trade frequency since valid mean reversion setups should already have ADX<25.
insight.risks: ADX can oscillate around 25 in transitional regimes, potentially blocking some valid setups. Mitigated by keeping the ADX<25 scoring bonus — only trades that genuinely qualify for the regime confirmation point will have ADX clearly below threshold.

current_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.
proposed_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 25, regime is TRENDING or BUILDING TREND — do NOT take mean reversion signals. ADX 20–25 is borderline; require at least one additional oversold signal (RSI<35 or BelowBB) before entering. ADX < 20 is the preferred ranging regime for mean reversion entries.
